orders.text:
WPSS No. 193 of 2016 
Hon’ble U.C. Dhyani, J. 
Mr. C.S. Rawat, Advocate for the 
petitioner. 
Mr. A.K. Joshi, Addl. C.S.C. for the 
State/respondents. 
By means of present writ petition, the 
petitioner seeks following reliefs among others: 
(i) Issue a writ, order or direction in the 
nature of certiorari to quash the impugned order 
dated 07.01.2016 passed by respondent no. 5 
(Contained as Annexure no. 3 to this writ 
petition). 
 (ii) Issue a writ, order or direction in the 
nature of mandamus directing the respondents to 
regularized the services of the petitioners in the 
light of Regularization Rules framed by the State 
Government time to time or give parity to other 
similarly situated incumbents (Annexure no. 7 of 
the writ petition). 
(iii) Issue a writ, order or direction in the 
nature of mandamus direct the respondents to pay 
the minimum pay alongwith dearness allowance 
to the petitioners as are being paid to regularly 
appointed employees in the State of Uttarakhand. 
(iv) Issue a writ, order or direction in the 
nature of mandamus directing the respondents to 
make payment of arrears of dearness allowance to 
the petitioners.  As prayed, four weeks time is granted 
to the learned counsel for the respondents to 
file counter affidavit. 
List this writ petition after four weeks. 
Urgency application (IA no. 682/2016) 
as well as stay application (CLMA no. 
789/2016) stand disposed of. 
 (U.C. Dhyani, J.) 
 Vacation Judge
 03.02.2016 Pooja

WPSS No.193 of 2016
Hon’ble Rajiv Sharma, J.
Mr. C.S. Rawat, Advocate for the 
petitioners. 
Mr. N.P.Sah, Standing Counsel 
for the State. 
The petitioners were the 
employees of the State Government. 
Thereafter, their services were engaged 
through Contractor after 2002. The 
petitioners have approached this 
Court. This Court directed the State 
Government to frame a policy. 
The State Government, till date, 
has not framed any policy despite 
mandatory directions issued by this 
Court. 
Accordingly, the writ petition is 
disposed of with the direction to the 
respondents to consider to frame a 
Policy within a period of six weeks 
from today, which would govern the 
petitioners and similarly situate 
persons for their regularization by 
counting their services which they 
have rendered with the State 
Government for more than 10-15 
years. 
All pending applications stand 
disposed of. 
 (Rajiv Sharma, J.) 
01.05.2017 
Jitendra

 Versus

Hon’ble Pankaj Purohit, J.
Mr. C.S. Rawat, learned counsel for the 
petitioners.
2. Mr. G.S. Negi, learned Additional C.S.C. for 
the State.
3. There is a conflict between the petitioners’ 
version and the respondent/State’s version. 
Petitioners are claiming that they have been 
working with the department for the last 20 to 40 
years, while the version of the State is that the 
petitioners, though working since long, are now 
working through a Contractor, but the 
respondent/State is not in a position to say as to 
when the petitioners were engaged through the 
Contractor.
4. In such view of the matter, State is directed 
to file supplementary counter affidavit specifying 
the date since when the petitioners were engaged 
through the Contractor or as to whether they are 
still working or not.
5. List on 02.11.2026.
(Pankaj Purohit, J.)
29.09.2026 AK
